subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: the sensor that sits in brain tissue and records the electrical spikes of individual neurons.
parts: flexible polymer threads or silicon shanks

subsystems.name: Implant electronics
subsystems.role: amplifies, digitises and packages the tiny neural signals.

subsystems.name: Power and telemetry
subsystems.role: lets the implant work without wires through the skin.

subsystems.name: Surgical insertion system
subsystems.role: places fragile electrodes precisely while avoiding blood vessels.

subsystems.name: Decoding software
subsystems.role: turns patterns of neuron firing into intended movements or commands.

subsystems.name: External effector
subsystems.role: the device the user controls — a cursor, robotic arm or their own stimulated muscles.

buildSteps.title: Design the array and chip
buildSteps.detail: Engineers decide how many electrodes, how deep and what materials, then design a custom chip that fits the power and heat budget.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate electrodes
buildSteps.detail: In a cleanroom, thin films of metal and polymer are patterned into dozens or hundreds of microelectrodes on flexible threads or silicon shanks.

buildSteps.title: Build the implant
buildSteps.detail: The chip is mounted in a sealed case, connected to the electrodes and tested for leaks and electrical noise.

buildSteps.title: Preclinical testing
buildSteps.detail: Devices are implanted in animals for months to check biocompatibility, signal quality and how scar tissue forms around the electrodes.

buildSteps.title: Plan the surgery
buildSteps.detail: A high-resolution MRI maps the patient's brain so the surgeon can target the motor cortex and avoid blood vessels.

buildSteps.title: Implant with a robot
buildSteps.detail: A small opening is made in the skull; a robot inserts each thread or array into the cortex at a controlled speed.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the decoder
buildSteps.detail: The patient imagines specific movements while software learns which neural patterns correspond to each intention.

buildSteps.title: Use and maintain
buildSteps.detail: The user controls a computer or limb wirelessly, charging the implant inductively and receiving software updates.

prerequisites.why: signals fade over months to years as scar tissue forms around stiff or moving electrodes.
an implant must survive salt water and immune attack for a decade or more.
hundreds of channels of neural data must stream through intact skin without wires.
decoders must be accurate, low-latency and stable as the brain changes.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory and ethical framework for brain implants
prerequisites.why: rules for long-term implants, privacy and enhancement are still being written.

pathway.milestone: early human trials for paralysis, including Neuralink's first implant in 2024 and academic trials such as BrainGate
pathway.unlocks: proof that people can control computers and simple devices with decoded neural signals.

pathway.milestone: larger trials for speech, vision and finer motor control
pathway.unlocks: clinical evidence across more patients and conditions.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval for specific medical indications
pathway.unlocks: routine use in rehabilitation for severe paralysis or locked-in syndrome.
speculative; no reliable evidence yet that implants can safely improve memory or intelligence in healthy people.
